newsitem.title: CHINA: Visa to connect with 1,028 ATMs in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Visa to connect with 1,028 ATMs in Shanghai.

text.p: Visa International on Tuesday received the official Chinese green light for its Visa and Visa/Plus cards to draw Chinese currency from 1,028 automatic telling machines (ATM) in Shanghai, the company said.
By the end of 1997, its new Golden Card Network would connect all Shanghai's ATMs, currently numbering 1,028, it said.

Visa, the world's biggest credit card organisation, and the Shanghai Credit Card Network received the go-ahead last June for the Golden Card Network from Shanghai's city government and the local central bank branch, it said.

Shanghai branches of Visa member banks included the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, the Bank of Communications, the Agricultural Bank of China and the Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, the company statement said.
Already, 100 ATMS had been connected to the network, which was designed for the convenience of foreigners in Shanghai who wanted local currency, it said.
Shanghai was the first step in the company's plans to extend the network throughout China, a source close to Visa said.
